requirements: The Admin can add, edit, and remove student information, including name, date of birth, and contact details, from the student database.
Teachers can assign grades to students for specific assignments and exams, which are then stored in the student's transcript.
Students can view their own grades and transcripts online, with the ability to filter by course and semester.
The system allows Parents to receive automated email notifications when their child's grades are updated or when assignments are due.
Teachers can generate attendance reports for their classes, showing which students were present or absent on a given day.
The system enables Admins to create and manage student schedules, including class assignments and room numbers.
Students can use the system to register for courses and sections for upcoming semesters, with the ability to select preferred instructors and class times.
The system allows Teachers to post announcements and assignments for their classes, which are then visible to students and parents.
The system must be able to handle a minimum of 10,000 concurrent student logins during peak registration periods without a decrease in performance.
All student data must be backed up nightly, with backups stored offsite for disaster recovery purposes, to ensure business continuity in the event of a system failure.
The system must comply with FERPA regulations regarding student data privacy and security, including encryption of sensitive data both in transit and at rest.
The system's user interface must be accessible on a variety of devices, including desktops, laptops, tablets, and smartphones, to accommodate different user preferences and needs.
The system must be able to integrate with existing student information systems, such as library and cafeteria management systems, to provide a seamless user experience.

requirements: Teachers can submit final grades for students via a weighted rubric interface where each assignment category (e.g., exams, quizzes, projects) contributes a pre-configured percentage to the final grade.
Students can view their academic progress through a dashboard that displays GPA trends, completed credits, and upcoming course deadlines with color-coded urgency indicators.
Parents can receive automated weekly progress reports via email, summarizing their child's attendance, grades, and teacher feedback without requiring manual requests.
The Registrar can generate degree audit reports that highlight missing requirements for graduation by cross-referencing student transcripts with the official curriculum checklist.
Counselors can flag students for academic intervention by attaching a risk assessment score (e.g., low attendance, failing grades) that triggers an automated alert to the student’s advisor.
Students can submit graduation petitions online, which are routed to the Registrar for approval and automatically update their academic status in the system.
Teachers can upload assignment rubrics in PDF format that are embedded directly into the student portal for transparency in grading criteria.
The system must enforce course prerequisites by preventing students from enrolling in advanced courses unless they have completed the required prior courses with a minimum grade threshold.
The system must support concurrent access by up to 5,000 users during peak enrollment periods without degrading response time below 2 seconds for grade submission queries.
All student data must be encrypted at rest using AES-256 and in transit via TLS 1.3 to comply with FERPA regulations for educational records.
The grade submission interface must be accessible via screen readers and keyboard navigation to accommodate users with disabilities, adhering to WCAG 2.1 AA standards.
The system must retain academic records for a minimum of 5 years after a student’s last enrollment, with automated archival to cold storage after 3 years of inactivity.
The final grade submission workflow must include a 30-second auto-save feature to prevent data loss in case of network interruptions during high-traffic periods.

risk_report.stage: Requirements Finalization and FERPA Compliance Review
risk_report.risk: Incomplete or ambiguous requirements may lead to compliance gaps or scope creep.
risk_report.mitigation: Conduct thorough stakeholder reviews and formalize requirements with clear FERPA compliance checkpoints.

risk_report.stage: System Architecture Design and Scalability Planning
risk_report.risk: Poor scalability design may cause performance bottlenecks under high user loads.
risk_report.mitigation: Implement modular architecture with horizontal scaling capabilities and load testing early.

risk_report.stage: Database Schema Design and Encryption Strategy
risk_report.risk: Inefficient schema or weak encryption may lead to data breaches or performance issues.
risk_report.mitigation: Use normalized schema with encryption at rest and in transit, validated by security reviews.

risk_report.stage: User Interface and Accessibility Design (WCAG 2.1 AA)
risk_report.risk: Non-compliance with WCAG 2.1 AA may result in legal issues or exclusion of disabled users.
risk_report.mitigation: Engage accessibility experts early and conduct iterative testing with assistive technologies.

risk_report.stage: API and Integration Design for Third-Party Systems
risk_report.risk: Poorly designed APIs may cause integration failures or security vulnerabilities.
risk_report.mitigation: Adopt RESTful standards with strict input validation and OAuth 2.0 for third-party access.

risk_report.risk: Inadequate security controls may expose sensitive student data to breaches.
risk_report.mitigation: Implement defense-in-depth with regular audits and automated compliance checks.

risk_report.stage: Backend Services Development (Grade Submission, Rubric Upload, etc.)
risk_report.risk: Bugs in critical workflows may corrupt or mishandle grade data.
risk_report.mitigation: Use TDD and peer reviews for core services with automated regression testing.

risk_report.risk: Frontend bugs may break accessibility or user workflows, reducing adoption.
risk_report.mitigation: Adopt component-based frameworks with automated accessibility and unit tests.

risk_report.stage: Automated Email and Notification System (Weekly Reports, Alerts)
risk_report.risk: Failed or delayed notifications may lead to missed deadlines or compliance violations.
risk_report.mitigation: Implement retry logic, monitoring, and fallback mechanisms for email services.

risk_report.stage: Degree Audit and Prerequisite Enforcement Logic
risk_report.risk: Incorrect audit logic may allow invalid degree progressions, violating academic policies.
risk_report.mitigation: Validate logic with academic stakeholders and use formal verification for critical paths.

risk_report.stage: Data Archival and Retention Policy Implementation
risk_report.risk: Non-compliance with retention policies may result in legal penalties or data leaks.
risk_report.mitigation: Automate archival with encryption and enforce policy via database triggers and audits.

risk_report.stage: Load Testing and Performance Optimization for 5,000 Concurrent Users
risk_report.risk: Undiscovered performance issues may crash the system during peak usage.
risk_report.mitigation: Conduct load testing early with realistic data and optimize bottlenecks iteratively.

risk_report.stage: Unit and Integration Testing for All Modules
risk_report.risk: Insufficient test coverage may allow defects to reach production unnoticed.
risk_report.mitigation: Enforce 80%+ coverage with CI/CD pipelines and automated test reporting.

risk_report.stage: Accessibility and WCAG 2.1 AA Compliance Testing
risk_report.risk: Late discovery of accessibility issues may require costly rework.
risk_report.mitigation: Integrate accessibility testing into the CI pipeline and use automated tools alongside manual reviews.

risk_report.stage: Security Penetration Testing and FERPA Audit
risk_report.risk: Undetected vulnerabilities may lead to data breaches or regulatory fines.
risk_report.mitigation: Engage third-party security firms and conduct FERPA-specific audits before deployment.

risk_report.risk: Misaligned expectations may result in rejection of the system post-deployment.
risk_report.mitigation: Involve end-users early in iterative prototypes and define clear UAT acceptance criteria.

risk_report.stage: Production Environment Setup and Deployment Pipeline
risk_report.risk: Configuration errors may cause downtime or data loss during deployment.
risk_report.mitigation: Use infrastructure-as-code and blue-green deployments with rollback capabilities.

risk_report.stage: Gradual Rollout and Monitoring for Grade Submission Workflow
risk_report.risk: Uncontrolled rollout may expose critical workflows to untested edge cases.
risk_report.mitigation: Deploy to a small cohort first with real-time monitoring and rapid incident response.

risk_report.stage: Final Documentation and Training for All User Roles
risk_report.risk: Inadequate training may lead to user errors or low adoption rates.
risk_report.mitigation: Develop role-specific guides and conduct live training sessions with feedback loops.

risk_report.risk: Unresolved performance issues may degrade user trust and system reliability.
risk_report.mitigation: Establish a dedicated support team and monitor key performance metrics continuously.
